test: joint Poisson (series + cluster x month effects)
evidence: 49% of what all drivers explain; top vs bottom third of months +16% volume-weighted; 62% of series same sign. By customer: Blinkit 3.1, Zepto 3.7, Instamart 1.8. Large cities only.

metric: offtake share of product within cluster x customer x month
grain: product x cluster x customer x month
evidence: About nine tenths of discount's effect is moving share between products of a cell; a higher average discount does not reliably lift the cell total (monthly average discount vs monthly offtake: correlation 0.08).
8% of what drivers explain. Moves with listing (correlation 0.80): credit is shared between the two.

effect_unit: % vs baseline when OSA < 40% or falls 20+ points
evidence: Offtake 20-33% under baseline in the stock-out month, recovers the month after. About 6% of series-months; most often Instamart.
4% of what drivers explain; strongest on Instamart (2.3% per point). Listing falling 20+ points: offtake about 45% under.
3% of what drivers explain jointly, but the largest one-at-a-time lift (+49% volume-weighted). May partly follow sales rather than drive them. Not plannable.
3% of what drivers explain; 55% of values are zero; strongest on Blinkit (2.5% per point).

grain: cluster x place x customer x month
test: one at a time + joint + cell growth
evidence: No relation over time within a series (correlation 0.00). Positive readings come only from comparing customers and are not stable between periods. Count jumps in May 2025 because the file starts covering small cities.
Total peaks Jun, lowest Nov (3.3x). Cluster shapes differ a lot: Delhi 6.0x, UP 8.5x, Rajasthan 7.7x vs Kerala 2.0x, Mumbai-Pune 2.2x. Each month rests on one or two readings.
Blinkit 4.7x, Zepto 3.4x, Instamart 2.6x. A back-test showed these are mostly share shifts between customers, not different seasons.

Other places went from about 5% of offtake (2024) to about a quarter (early 2026); growth comes in steps, not at a steady pace. Over half of offtake in several clusters (e.g. Punjab-Haryana-Hills, Greater Maharashtra).
Blinkit +120%, Zepto +98%, Instamart -12% (stable). Blinkit's growth is not discount-led (its discount fell to 3-5% from Nov 2025).
Selected in 9 of 9 fully estimated fits but in 1 of 9 once the cluster seasonal index is in: the season already carries most of it.

driver: festivals (Diwali / Eid / Durga Puja / Onam / Ganesh Chaturthi)
evidence: Durga Puja, Onam, Ganesh Chaturthi dropped in every fit; Diwali kept in 9 of 21 (negative), Eid in 8 of 21 (positive, probably the start-of-season ramp).

effect_unit: % change in ECO % (first vs second half of history)
evidence: Cabinets +151% while active cabinets +79%: added cabinets are activated at a lower rate. SS: cabinets up sharply since 2023 while SS ECO % fell each year.
Volume tracks active cabinets (0.95) far more than total cabinets (0.71); throughput was flat (+4%, not significant). Growth came from more active cabinets, not more per cabinet.
Cluster is the only grouping that changes the seasonal shape. Channel, supply format, FU and tier do not (p = 1.0). Company peak Apr, trough Dec; cluster peaks Apr to Jun.

effect_unit: coefficient of variation of the month's ratio across years
evidence: Apr and May are the least reliable months (volume CV 35-40%, ECO count 29-35%, throughput 12-20%); Nov and Aug the most reliable. A big Apr-May gap vs normal is less unusual than the same gap in Nov.
Channel and supply format decide how fast volume grows (geography decides when it peaks). Tier also differs (0.31) but may be confounded with cluster or launch recency.

Cluster totals, all months, raw temperature: about 0.09 after removing the season (raw 0.76 only because both are seasonal). Highest Mumbai-Pune 0.25, Karnataka 0.24, Greater Maharashtra 0.18; Kerala -0.12. Too coarse to rule weather out: see C07 and T01.

All months: mostly under 0.3. Apr-May only: 0.4-0.8 for many BP x cluster pairs (e.g. Tamil Nadu tubs about 0.7; several BPs in Greater Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh 0.6-0.8), but n = 8 readings per pair and raw temperature, not anomaly. Signal looks concentrated in the peak and at finer grain.
Cluster totals, all months: between -0.15 and +0.07 after removing the season. Not tested at finer grain or as anomalies.
Near zero after removing the season; festival-day counts are almost fixed by calendar month, so they repeat the season. Major-festival lift by cluster not yet tested (T02).

grain: channel x cluster x month (and bp x cluster); peak months separately
evidence: The test that matters: anomaly vs the same calendar month's normal, by channel x cluster, on ECO % and throughput separately, peak (Mar-Jun) and other months apart. Weather table (cluster x month, 2019-2026, with anomalies and hot days) is ready.

evidence: Lift in months with the event vs without, by cluster and channel; festival calendar by cluster and custom events table are ready.
